title: Cops Realize Psycho Daughters Car Is Filled With Bodies

beats.description: Cold open: Officers confront Cassandra at motel, mention three family members found dead and burned.
Narrator sets up the case: routine Friday, Kane's first 911 calls about squatters and missing grandmother.
Mike Fledge reports Kane as suspicious and armed; Sergeant Nordquist begins welfare check.
First welfare check finds house empty and staged; Kane cancels check; Nordquist calls Kane, notes lies.
Burned vehicle found with three bodies; officers identify it as Victor's Subaru; homicide suspected.
Autopsy confirms victims; Kane's wife Samantha reveals domestic violence and a recording.
Second search of house finds blood spatter, shell casings, cleanup supplies; evidence of multiple perpetrators.
Detectives inform Mike and Lourdes of deaths; Lourdes identifies Cassandra as potential accomplice.
Cassandra calls 911 claiming Kane is missing; officers visit her house, unaware Kane is hiding inside.
Neighbors report Kane staying with Cassandra; Walmart footage shows them buying bleach and kerosene.
Search warrant executed at Cassandra's house; officers find basement with victim documents and ammunition.
Phone ping places Cassandra in Mississippi; officers confront her at motel; she slips up about knowing victims are dead.
Kane voluntarily walks into Mississippi police station; interview begins with Agent Silva.
Kane claims Mike shot at him; Silva debunks with no bullet holes or camera evidence.
Silva presses Kane on texts with Cassandra; Kane shows no emotion, leading officers to suspect he knew.
Green Subaru found with Kane's passport, gloves, ammo; Kane arrested for murder.
Cassandra flees back to New Mexico; detectives interview her at parents' house, she begins to confess.
Cassandra admits helping clean up blood and move bodies; implicates Kane as primary actor.
Final interrogation: Agent Graham confronts Kane with Cassandra's confession; Kane admits to covering up murders.
Kane claims Victor and Killian shot each other; Graham dismisses story; Kane requests attorney.
Charges filed: Kane with three counts murder, arson; Cassandra with murder, conspiracy, tampering.
Narrator summarizes evidence and motive: property dispute over 22 acres; both face life sentences.
Closing remarks: family can rest; case remains presumed innocent until trial.
